subject.title: fix(clickclack): add timeouts to REST client requests

question: Should ClickClack apply an unconditional 30-second completion deadline to all JSON REST reads and mutating calls while leaving multipart FormData uploads unbounded?
rationale: The patch correctly implements one coherent policy, but current main has no REST completion deadline and the timeout can change behavior for existing slow API operations; source and tests cannot choose that user-facing operational contract.

options.title: Approve the owner-local 30-second policy
options.body: Accept bounded failure for all ClickClack JSON REST operations and retain the multipart-upload exemption, then refresh the branch and merge.

options.title: Use an operation-specific deadline policy
options.body: Ask for a narrowed revision that distinguishes request classes or supplies a compatible alternative before the new deadline applies broadly.

options.title: Defer the change
options.body: Keep the current unbounded REST behavior until ClickClack’s latency and retry contract is defined more broadly.

recommendation.title: Approve the owner-local 30-second policy
recommendation.body: Accept bounded failure for all ClickClack JSON REST operations and retain the multipart-upload exemption, then refresh the branch and merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion directly requests this product-contract decision from steipete, while the closest landed implementation precedent is a separate WebSocket timeout change.
